entries.claim: The mount steers the occupant while the mount clip plays (FUN_005b3340, the one-shot branch): toward origin + R(gun yaw at the mount) x (refPt + the clip root's travel so far), the skel_root's x and z zeroed (its y the last pose's), the whole offset times sqrt(ease(phase)) a tick at the motion's own phase, 0 to (n - 1)/n (ease 2p^2 to the half, 1 - 2(p - 1)^2 after), unclamped; refPt moved after each tick's offset by the clip root's velocity x dt (the key pair's change x keys / playback); the facing turned toward the gun's yaw at the mount -- the gun part's flattened forward, where its last occupant left it (the room's TurretState.gunYaw, the page's drawn aim) -- at 2 pi rad/s at most times the sine of the angle; never abandoned for distance. The clip comes off at the driver's end test before the tick's advance (the stored phase plus half a game frame's step past (n - 1)/n): 16 steer ticks at 60 Hz (key 24.04; 8 at the game's frame, key 24.06), and the hold places the body and lays the gun's facing on that same tick (the room and the page alike). The steer leaves the feet 0.215 from the hold's place at 60 Hz (0.293 at the game's frame) on Crossroads' two and Vigilance's four turrets; the steer meets no polygon wall, the gun's own hull included, in the room and on the page alike (T81-4: FUN_005483d0 restores the move's unresolved displacement in the turret anim set; was: the room's walk stopped them 2.43 short and the hold placed them). The height is the floor's after each move: the steer's vertical takes the body through no floor. Nothing parents the actor to a node of the turret's rig; the room lays the turn as the command's yaw (emplacements.mount.seat-turn).
